scope: Life (inoti.ks), camp stories and the separate earlier-generation body-rental branch. Preserve this game's chronology and visiting-student continuity.
policy: Given-name-first English; established names and source kana are locked. Two idol surname readings remain provisional. Preserve ambiguity, named bodies, apparent identities and speaker labels separately.

entries.role: Student and missing camper; skilled pendant maker
entries.voice_and_context: Student in the camp story more than twenty years earlier. Explicitly a boy at494 and parents call him their son1248–1250. His recorded speech is identified at559. Reiko calls him a self-proclaimed bullying victim; her hostile judgments are narration, not independent facts. Missing outcome differs by branch.
entries.note: Do not invent cause of disappearance. First camp branch suggests Reiko’s mother possesses the pendant; rental-body branch changes events.

entries.role: All-boys-school student; Reiko’s online friend
entries.voice_and_context: One of three boys from an all-boys school in Nakano, Tokyo. Says he has lived fifteen years without a girlfriend and is a virgin. Frightened of women and fixated on losing his virginity.
entries.note: His age15 is stated; do not automatically assign it to the other two.

entries.role: All-boys-school student; musician; Reiko’s online friend
entries.voice_and_context: Member of the male trio. Outgoing flirt, plays in a rock band and invites Reiko to a school-festival performance. Often ends boasts with baby.

entries.role: All-boys-school student; comedian’s son; Reiko’s online friend
entries.voice_and_context: Member of male trio. His father is an unnamed famous comedian; celebrity acquaintances and paternal influence are discussed, not a named father.
entries.note: Do not identify the unnamed father with a real comedian.

entries.role: Mysterious woman; claimed/apparent university student
entries.voice_and_context: One of three apparently female university students met for fireworks. Tells an uncertain story of alien experiments and teases that she may be the Slit-Mouthed Woman. Tsuzuki speculates their names are hostess working names; Koreeda speculates all three are slit-mouthed women.
entries.note: University status, hostess status, supernatural identity and assumed alias status are not all confirmed.

entries.role: Mysterious woman; claimed/apparent university student
entries.voice_and_context: Woman in Kaname’s trio. Enthusiastic about celebrity photographs and flirts with younger Tsuzuki.
entries.note: Same uncertain hostess/alias/supernatural claims as Kaname.

entries.role: Mysterious woman; claimed/apparent university student
entries.voice_and_context: Woman in Kaname’s trio. Bluntly insults Moriyama and kicks him away from Kaname.
entries.note: Same uncertain hostess/alias/supernatural claims as Kaname.

entries.role: Student; delinquent; online acquaintance
entries.voice_and_context: Tokyo all-boys-school student, one of two violent delinquents Reiko knows through online gaming. Polite speech contrasts with prostitution brokering, diverted drugs, extortion and violence. Boats with Saito and later attacks him while seeing a girl’s ghost.

entries.role: Student; delinquent; online acquaintance
entries.voice_and_context: Other delinquent in boat story. His image is superimposed with an unnamed dead girl; source speaker label stays his name. Survives the beating but remains unconscious at ending.
entries.note: The ghost girl is not Saito’s ordinary identity.

entries.role: Swimming instructor; reportedly elementary-school PE teacher
entries.voice_and_context: Pool/swimming-area instructor, described as an elementary-school PE teacher in his ordinary job. All instructors explicitly male3940. Nicknamed シラミ, an insult meaning louse. Possible collusion in Nozawa’s drowning remains Reiko’s inference.
entries.note: Nicknameシラミ is distinct from the proper surname and must retain insulting wordplay. Do not make rumored collusion an omniscient confirmed motive.

entries.role: Camper; swimming-group companion
entries.voice_and_context: Girl who forms a three-girl swimming group with Reiko and Nozawa, then restrains Reiko during Nozawa’s apparent drowning and dictates the account that she went home. Reiko suspects a link with Shiraki but does not prove it.
entries.note: Unknown exact motive/organization affiliation; no definitive identification of underwater figure.

entries.role: Camper; middle-school girl in remembered incident
entries.voice_and_context: Girl in Reiko/Manami swimming group. Starts with surname-only address; later invites first-name friendship. Claims her father is instructor’s employer, then explicitly admits her family has no connection to camp operator.
entries.note: Do not label her a company president’s daughter or heiress as fact; that is a retracted bluff.

entries.role: Camper; Adventure companion; eventual swimmer in one branch
entries.voice_and_context: Girl Reiko’s age at Adventure activity. Her older sister, an unnamed promising swimmer, died in an accident; mother pressures Yoko to follow her. In one ending Yoko becomes an outstanding female swimmer. Sister’s locker-room ghost is distinct from Yoko.
entries.note: Do not identify her dead older sister by Yoko’s given name.

entries.role: Fortune-teller / camp instructor / self-styled queen
entries.voice_and_context: Self-described proprietor of a fortune-telling hall who works as camp Adventure instructor in summer. Plays Queen Miwako of the subterranean kingdom; old-fashioned imperious speech is deliberate. A fortune-teller-clothed mummy is found in one ending but not explicitly named as Miwako.
entries.note: Queen title belongs to camp performance, not independently established actual state. Mummy identification remains implied, not explicit.

entries.role: Camper; later actress; body occupied in rental story
entries.voice_and_context: Older-generation camper who demands Onuma’s pendant; later described as a popular actress. Closing bus conversation retains her speaker label, but Hanae calls her Haraguchi and the occupant says this is the body wanted from the start.
entries.note: Do not infer Laura versus Lola solely fromローラ. Keep physical/speaker identity distinct from claimed occupant Haraguchi. Rola is the project Latin spelling of the explicit kana; no Laura/Lola derivation is asserted.
entries.reading_status: Explicit native kana7141; Rola is the chosen project Latin spelling

entries.role: Camper with ancestral-spirit protection; apparent older-generation story source
entries.voice_and_context: Older-generation camper and companion of Aoki, nicknamed Hana. Detects unusual speech/occupant and says ancestral spirits warn of danger. Closing story source is Reiko’s friend Motoki Sanae’s mother, strongly suggesting but not literally naming Hanae as that mother.
entries.note: Do not conflate葉苗 and早苗. Hana nickname is not a separate character. Wiki explicitly identifies Sanae as her daughter. Preserve the script's order of disclosure rather than adding this fact early.

entries.role: Transfer student presentation; mysterious body renter
entries.voice_and_context: Says newly transferred at end of first term; appears unusually small for high school. Claims body rental/takeover. Implied to occupy Onuma before Aoki, with closing dialogue explicit about occupying Aoki’s body. Reiko wonders whether Haraguchi is an alien.
entries.note: Alien identity is a question7420, not confirmed. Do not collapse speaker/body labels into one fixed person. Wiki treats the presented character as a girl, but the actual body-renting occupant's identity remains unresolved; do not import the other game's biography.

entries.role: Reiko’s close friend with spiritual sensitivity
entries.voice_and_context: Reiko’s close friend. Story source is this friend’s mother. Said to talk with ancestral spirits. Same surname as Hanae, but different given name.
entries.note: Mother is not explicitly named in7422–7424; relationship to Hanae is contextual.

entries.reading_status: Provisional working surname reading; no game-specific kana found. Do not substitute real-world idols.
